title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Excess Withdrawal Fees Owed and Where They Fall
content:
Once a Savings & Money Market Accounts product's statement cycle has been set against the withdrawals it counts, two things remain to be fixed: how many excess withdrawal fees are still due, and which withdrawal carries each one. This page states how both are fixed.

## Rule

**Fees due.** Start from the counted withdrawals past the allowance that carry no standing fee: the number past the allowance less the number already carrying one. The fees due are that figure or the capacity left under the per-cycle maximum, whichever is smaller, and never fewer than none.

**Amount.** Each fee due is set at the excess withdrawal fee of the account's tier, rounded half-up to the cent.

**Placement.** Where one or more fees are due, one is charged on the earliest counted withdrawal past the allowance, in posting order, that has no fee on it, as a single fee entry of that cycle naming that withdrawal as its source item. Every further fee due is its own entry of the same amount, placed on the next such withdrawal in turn.

**None due.** Where no fee is due, the policy charges nothing.

## Worked example (hypothetical cycle)

Ten counted withdrawals against a free allowance assumed to be 6, so four lie past it (the 7th to the 10th). The cycle already holds three excess fee entries: on the 7th and 8th counted withdrawals, and one on a branch cash withdrawal that has since been refunded as a bank error. Take the per-cycle maximum as 6.

- Carrying a standing fee: three entries less one bank-error refund, so two.
- Past the allowance with no standing fee: four less two, so two.
- Capacity left: six less three, so three.
- Fees due: the smaller of two and three, so two.
- Placement: one fee on the 9th counted withdrawal and one on the 10th.

With a capacity of one, only the 9th would be charged.

## Points of judgement

**Could more fees be due than withdrawals lie past the allowance?** No. Standing fees can only shrink that number, and the capacity can only shrink it further.
